findings.original_claim: ROS formula is Operating Profit / Net Sales while coursebook uses Net Income / Revenue.
findings.required_change: Label coursebook ROS/net profit margin = net income / revenue, multiplying by 100 for percent. Add: Operating-profit-based return on sales is a different convention; identify numerator before comparing firms. Cite edo-3-2-4-cost-price-evaluation-2025 pp17-18.
findings.source_basis: Coursebook pp16-18 visible statement and calculations
findings.explanation: Aligns drill calculation without claiming finance has only one ROS definition.

findings.original_claim: Fully burdened labor rate always includes profit/fee; example $34/hr contains only costs.
findings.guide_location: Formula block and Fully Burdened Rate
findings.required_change: Separate: Burdened cost rate = (direct labor + applicable allocated indirect costs)/labor hours. A quoted billing/price rate may add profit/fee; specify basis. The coursebook examples use cost-only $63.25/hr (6325/100) and $34/hr (1.7M/50000). Cost estimate = hours x matching cost rate; avoid adding overhead or fee twice. Cite coursebook pp36-38 and p40.
findings.source_basis: Coursebook p36 prose conflicts with explicit p37 formula/table and p38 exercise
findings.explanation: Preserve cost/price distinction and correct numerical learning objective.

findings.original_claim: Indirect rate formulas lack worked allocation and explicit G&A rate formula.
findings.guide_location: Indirect Cost Pools, Bases, and Rates
findings.required_change: Add: OH rate = 2000/1500 = 133.333%; for direct labor A750/B500/C250 allocate OH1000/666.67/333.33, totaling2000. Total costs are1750/1166.67/583.33. With direct50k + OH100k, TCI150k; G&A15k/TCI150k =10%, total cost165k before fee. Round only final allocations. Cite coursebook pp32-35.
findings.explanation: Completes explicit calculation TLO5a/b; guide previously only formula-level coverage.

findings.original_claim: Balance sheet and income statement names described but no relationships.
findings.required_change: Add: Assets = liabilities + owners' equity; current liabilities are near-term obligations. Revenue less costs/expenses yields successive gross, operating and net results. Use the stated net-income line and consistent period/asset basis for the coursebook ratios; profitability does not by itself prove liquidity or responsibility. Cite coursebook pp15-19.
findings.explanation: Makes diagram teaching accessible in prose.

findings.original_claim: Practitioner Steps says price first then cost only if price insufficient.
findings.required_change: Use: Perform price analysis to assess the total price. Perform cost analysis when certified cost or pricing data are required, and as needed for other-data cases when price analysis alone cannot establish reasonableness. Use cost realism for contemplated cost-reimbursement awards. Cite FAR-Overhaul-Part15-2026,15.404.
findings.source_basis: Official RFO15.404(a) verified in parent live body
findings.explanation: Ensures procedural shortcut does not override required cost analysis.

notes: All41 slides inspected visually including p6 proposed-price tree, p8 detailed cost table, p15-18 financial statements/ratios, p27/31 cost breakdown, p33 overhead allocations, p34 TCI, p37 fully burdened-rate table.
Coursebook p8 has $10,500 computer engineer versus much larger comparators; it is a fact-finding anomaly, not silently corrected to $105,000. Arithmetic as printed ties.

Current certified-data threshold, CAS threshold, nontraditional exemption and TINA Lite changes were fully verified in preceding 2026-10-20 acquisition-policy audit and must be retained. This review does not duplicate that research or claim access to current signed DFARS Part215 attachment.
